Q: How to use the SORT statement with a 2D-table in COBOL? A:

The comments requesting a minimal, reproducible example and for which compiler and operating environment are correct and I recommend including this information in future questions. Omitting these often results in your question being closed without being answered.

Something else that is confusing is your statement "I need to use the SORT statement to sort TABLE-03 content by index, but this statement does not work with indexed elements." The terms "index" and "indexed" have very specific meanings in the context of a COBOL table.

You cannot sort TABLE-03 because the item you apparently wish to sort on, KEY-VAR, is in TABLE-05 and you cannot sort on a subscripted item. This is true of a standards-conforming compiler, absent an extension that allows this (and taking advantage of that would make your code non-portable).

I think what you're looking for is to sort each element of TABLE-03.

   Identification Division.
   Program-ID. SORT0001.
   Data Division.
   Working-Storage Section.
   01  WORK-AREAS.
       05  SUB-03 PIC 9999 COMP.
       05  SUB-05 PIC 9999 COMP.
       05  SUB-99 PIC 9999.
       
   01  TABLE-01.
       03  TABLE-03 OCCURS 5 TIMES.
           05  TABLE-05 OCCURS 10 TIMES.
               07  KEY-VAR PIC X(05).
               07  SM-ELEM PIC X(04).
   Procedure Division.
  * Load the table with some data
   PERFORM VARYING SUB-03 FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL SUB-03 > 5
     PERFORM VARYING SUB-05 FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL SUB-05 > 10
       MOVE SUB-03 TO SUB-99
       MOVE SUB-99(2:3) TO KEY-VAR(SUB-03,SUB-05)(1:3)
       MOVE SUB-05 TO SUB-99
       MOVE SUB-99(3:2) TO KEY-VAR(SUB-03,SUB-05)(4:2)
       MOVE SPACES TO SM-ELEM(SUB-03,SUB-05)
     END-PERFORM
   END-PERFORM

  * Sort each instance of TABLE-05
  * I'm using DESCENDING to show that the SORT 
  * actually worked
   PERFORM VARYING SUB-03 FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL SUB-03 > 5
     SORT TABLE-05(SUB-03) ON DESCENDING KEY-VAR
   END-PERFORM

  * Display the data
   PERFORM VARYING SUB-03 FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL SUB-03 > 5
     PERFORM VARYING SUB-05 FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL SUB-05 > 10
       DISPLAY 'KEY-VAR(' SUB-03 ',' SUB-05 ') ' 
         KEY-VAR(SUB-03,SUB-05)
     END-PERFORM
   END-PERFORM

   GOBACK.

Q: How to select a disk during an automated diskpart script? A:

I wasn't able to get Stephan's solution working without splitting up the commands into individual appends. I also delete the format.txt tool out of an abundance of caution, but it's probably not necessary as the > command should replace the contents.

@ECHO OFF
SETLOCAL ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION ENABLEEXTENSIONS
TITLE Windows Partition Prep Tool
IF EXIST format.txt del format.txt
>list.txt echo LIST DISK
diskpart /s list.txt
set /p "userchoice=Enter disk number: "
>format.txt echo SELECT DISK %userchoice%
>>format.txt echo CLEAN
>>format.txt echo CREATE PARTITION PRIMARY SIZE=1024
>>format.txt echo SELECT PARTITION 1
>>format.txt echo ACTIVE
>>format.txt echo FORMAT FS=FAT32 LABEL="PARAGON" QUICK
>>format.txt echo ASSIGN LETTER=P
>>format.txt echo CREATE PARTITION PRIMARY SIZE=952842
>>format.txt echo SELECT PARTITION 2
>>format.txt echo ACTIVE
>>format.txt echo FORMAT FS=NTFS LABEL="Backup" QUICK
>>format.txt echo ASSIGN LETTER=Q
diskpart /s format.txt

Q: SQL vs R : when to use which? A:

If you work or plan on working with a RDBMS, learn SQL fast and learn R later. In the 1980's and even in the 1990's SQL was seen as a replacement for Cobol (at least in my job it was). And even if you don't work with relational databases, SQL is still one of the most valuable tools you will have to solve real life problems.
If you want to work in data analysis and statistic models, R is much, much better. And plots are a part of both. R has base graphics, lattice graphics and ggplot2.

Q: Are there standard C# formatting conventions recommended for Unity development? A:

There is no real best common way. As usual this is extremely opinion and taste based. However, personally I would try to stick to general C# ways as much as possible as this allows to apply the same also to other C# contexts outside of Unity. You might want to make a couple of custom exceptions for e.g. differing between a private field and a serialized private field ... but most of the time it's fine to stick to standard C# conventions. I would NOT recommend to go by Unity's c++ like namings (m_, k_, s_, etc)

Q: Searching for strings in multiple text files and outputting matched lines to a CSV A:

Try openmode 'a' (append) rather than 'w' for the CSV.

Q: AWS DMS Keeps silently failing with resource temporarily unavailable (apr status = 11) A:

I had the same issue with RDS PostgreSQL 17.5. I was able to solve this when I changed my RDS version to PostgreSQL 15.13.

My guess is the version 17.5 has some unknown bugs causing this error. Try changing or downgrading the PostgreSQL version and see if that works.
